status: established_primary_source_consequence; no novelty or material validation claim

claim.exact_statement: For a sufficiently low-temperature nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising model on the periodic L-by-L square torus, with N=L^2 and dimensionless uniform field s, Borgs-Kotecky finite-size scaling implies that the one-site marginal at s=+c/N and s=-c/N has total-variation distance m_* tanh(m_* c)+o(1), uniformly for fixed c>0
claim.novelty_boundary: Borgs-Kotecky already prove the finite-size crossover; the local-calibration minimax consequence is a direct internal deduction. No novelty claim.
claim.costs: Uniform field precision O(epsilon/N) near coexistence; N independently uncertain local fields require that precision per coefficient in the coherent-error worst case. Local spin estimation from independent equilibrium shots costs O(epsilon^-2 log(1/delta)); equilibration/reset cost is unmeasured and can dominate.
claim.falsifier: A field-normalization mismatch, failure of the low-temperature contour assumptions, or an error in translating the magnetization separation into one-site TV would invalidate this transfer. A physical material failing the Ising interface blocks nature-level use.
claim.next_gate: Derive or reject a local calibration theorem under an acquired susceptibility/correlation-sum bound, then audit Dobrushin and cluster-expansion prior art before claiming novelty.
